details: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde has expressed strong skepticism regarding euro-denominated stablecoins, stating that their case is "far weaker than it appears." She warned that private stablecoins risk introducing fragility and fragmentation into tokenized financial markets, and relying on them for settlement could undermine interoperability.
title: ECB's Lagarde Skeptical of Euro Stablecoins, Cites Fragility Risks

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) warned in a May 7th blog post that advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) models are significantly enhancing cyber threats, potentially leading to systemic financial disruptions. The IMF highlighted how AI can accelerate the identification and exploitation of vulnerabilities within interconnected financial infrastructure, stressing the urgent need for improved resilience, supervision, and international coordination.
title: IMF: AI-Fueled Cyberattacks Threaten Global Financial Stability

details: Bitcoin's price slipped below $81,000 following reports that former US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's latest peace proposal, which escalated geopolitical tensions. This development put broader pressure on various risk assets, including cryptocurrencies. Despite the volatility, institutional investors have continued to accumulate Bitcoin, helping it maintain the crucial $80,000 support level.
title: Bitcoin Dips as Trump Rejects Iran Peace Deal, Geopolitical Tensions Rise

details: A recent Bloomberg survey indicates that money markets are pricing in expectations for the European Central Bank (ECB) to raise interest rates twice this year. Economists predict two 25 basis point hikes in June and September, driven by persistent inflation concerns, which have been exacerbated by the ongoing conflict in Iran.
title: ECB Expected to Hike Rates Twice This Year Amid Inflation Concerns
